title: Nonzero-point evaluations detect vector Laurent coefficients modulo a subspace
statement: Let $k$ be an infinite field [def-weil-field], let $r\geq0$ be an integer, let $V$ be a $k$-vector space of arbitrary dimension, and let $W\subseteq V$ be a $k$-linear subspace. A vector Laurent polynomial is a finite formal sum $P=\sum_{u\in\mathbf Z^r}v_uz^u$ with coefficients $v_u\in V$, all but finitely many zero. For $t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\in(k^\times)^r$ define $P(t)=\sum_u(\prod_{i=1}^rt_i^{u_i})v_u$. Then $P(t)\in W$ for every $t\in(k^\times)^r$ if and only if $v_u\in W$ for every $u\in\mathbf Z^r$. Empty sums and $r=0$ are allowed; in the latter case $\mathbf Z^0$ and $(k^\times)^0$ are singleton sets and the empty product is $1$.

proof.text: Let $S=\{u:v_u\ne0\}$, which is finite. If $S=\varnothing$, all coefficients and all evaluations are zero, so both conditions hold. Hence assume $S\ne\varnothing$. For the forward implication form $U=V/W$, the vector space of cosets with $[v]+[v\prime]=[v+v\prime]$ and $c[v]=[cv]$, and let $q(v)=[v]$. By the coset relation $q(v)=0$ exactly when $v\in W$. Linearity of $q$ gives $\sum_{u\in S}(\prod_i t_i^{u_i})q(v_u)=q(P(t))=0$ for every nonzero tuple $t$.

source.place: Proposition 1.11 and Remark 1.14, printed p.10; agent-written vector-coefficient and quotient argument spelling out joint injectivity.

proof.text: For each coordinate choose $a_i=1+\max(\{0\}\cup\{-u_i:u\in S\})$. Then $u_i+a_i\ge1$ for every $u\in S$. Given any linear map $\lambda:U\to k$, form the ordinary scalar polynomial $F_\lambda(X)=\sum_{u\in S}\lambda(q(v_u))\prod_i X_i^{u_i+a_i}$. At a tuple $x\in k^r$ having a zero coordinate every summand vanishes, since its exponent in that coordinate is positive. At a tuple with all coordinates nonzero, integer-power addition and linearity give $F_\lambda(x)=(\prod_i x_i^{a_i})\lambda(\sum_{u\in S}(\prod_i x_i^{u_i})q(v_u))=0$. Thus $F_\lambda$ vanishes on all of $k^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-mvpolynomial-infinite-evaluation] with $D=k$, variable set $\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and the zero polynomial; its infinite-domain hypothesis holds because $k$ is an infinite field. It yields $F_\lambda=0$. The shift $u\mapsto(u_i+a_i)_i$ is injective, so its coefficient at this shifted exponent is exactly $\lambda(q(v_u))$, which is therefore zero for each $u\in S$.

proof.text: Conversely, if every $v_u$ lies in $W$, each scalar multiple $(\prod_i t_i^{u_i})v_u$ belongs to $W$, and closure of a subspace under finite sums gives $P(t)\in W$. For $r=0$ the unique exponent gives a constant polynomial in no variables; step 2 has no zero-coordinate case and its empty product is $1$, so the same proof applies. The zero vector space and the subspaces $W=0$ and $W=V$ are included.
